quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely into traffic when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be prepared to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: More than 93 percent of fatal crashes are caused by ____ .
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers are not paying attention or do not follow the rules of the road. Being alert and obeying traffic laws are your most important responsibilities as a driver.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop your vehicle unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They get you ready for road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming, and you should prepare to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street. You should:

options.text: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep speeding up even if you take your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition with care—move it just enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: If you are in a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If you can, move your vehicle out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if someone is hurt. Do not move injured people unless necessary, but try to stop serious bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency workers to arrive.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, your tires need good tread and proper air pressure. Slow down when it rains because hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on this road. In rain, snow, ice, or other bad conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
So the buzzer or light does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn left—oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
It helps you find cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws.
It tells you about road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped warning signs have black symbols or words on yellow background. They alert you to conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: What is true about blind spots on larger vehicles?

options.text: They are the same size as on small vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What technique helps prevent crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to improve traction.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On snowy or icy roads, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. These are the most important ways to avoid crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let merging traffic in safely.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, flashing red lights mean a train is coming—wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on the left and a bicycle on the right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at once.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a full stop, yield the right-of-way, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the more impact force your vehicle has if it crashes.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. As a driver, you must stay alert for pedestrians and always yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop for other drivers or pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants in to the left. That shows that:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge marks where the road ends. When the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs indicate?

options.text: The speed you might drive in this area.
The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest and lowest speeds allowed on that road. These limits are for perfect conditions. You must drive slower when weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have lost control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is okay to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Honk to alert other drivers.

questions.question: What are the colors of signs that tell you the distance to the next exit on a highway?
questions.explanation: Highway information signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus completely on driving. Doing other tasks while driving is dangerous and distracting.

questions.question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, drive to the next one.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May continue through or exit from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the highway. You can change lanes to continue, or you must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: On slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes the road slippery. You may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions are not safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a playground is near. Watch for children in or near the roadway.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers you are entering.
Stick part of your car onto the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: When getting into a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: When should you drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes road conditions not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes road conditions not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit if the road is wet or slippery, if visibility is poor, or if anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is coming ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at that location.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its lights on and stop arm out, watch for children walking on the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you a curve is coming.

questions.question: When you see a yield sign at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield just to the traffic on the right.
Yield just to the traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic pass before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal medications, both prescription and over-the-counter. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This helps other drivers know your intentions and prevents accidents.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing at an intersection with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. Construction zones are dangerous for both drivers and workers. This sign tells drivers that penalties are greater for unsafe driving in work zones.

questions.question: Passing other vehicles is not allowed:
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal locations to pass.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, you should use ____ to show you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals are broken, use hand signals to tell other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is red, you must stop before the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: This sign marks a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles often cross or ride near traffic here.
